title: on Linux, bin/cairn keeps its floor and execs the Python dispatcher bin/cairn.py in place of its own 165 lines of dispatch
intention: After its floor checks, bin/cairn on Linux execs the venv python on bin/cairn.py (outline 5.4.3.8), so one dispatcher serves both platforms.
why: Measured: 2026-11-20 read of bin/cairn on akiendell: 479 lines, 295 of code; lines 94-217 are the bash floor (venv, db, wiring, instance), lines 218-313 the help, lines 314-479 the dispatch (token fold, instance split, device and bus resolution, exec). bin/proofs holds 34 proofs, 21 of which drive the launcher. This box cannot run a Linux read of them, so riding Linux on slice 1 (ticket 380d524e6e9c) is not cheap from here: it re-reads 21 proofs on a platform I do not hold. Owed by outline 5.4.3.8; the floor stays bash (5.4.3.8.1).
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured); Law 5 (the repo is the state of the machine: a crossing's record is committed where it lands); Law 9 (green is earned).
how: A hypothesis, not a settled shape: after 380d524e6e9c lands bin/cairn.py, bin/cairn keeps _floor and _help and replaces the dispatch block (line 314 on) with an exec of the venv python on bin/cairn.py with the same arguments. A parity proof resolves a fixed list of addresses (cc, cc.1, a bus verb, an unknown word, a case-folded token) through both and compares target and exit code. Depends on 380d524e6e9c. Depends on 80a220a86873: bin/cairn.py carries bootstrap.sh's instance wiring, so the exec drops none of it (measured 2026-11-20 on Windows: bash bin/cairn probescan wires 58 entries into an empty instance root, cairn.cmd 0).

clauses.claim: the 21 launcher-driving proofs in bin/proofs read green on Linux unchanged after bin/cairn execs bin/cairn.py
a fixed list of typed addresses resolves to the same target and exit code through the Python dispatcher as through the bash dispatch it replaced
bin/cairn holds no device or bus resolution of its own: its only exec after the floor is the Python dispatcher

on a fresh instance root, bin/cairn on Linux exec'ing bin/cairn.py leaves the same instance wiring bootstrap.sh's cairn_wire_instances laid before the exec (bin/cairn.py carries that wiring, ticket 80a220a86873)

decisions.text: D1: After its floor checks, bin/cairn on Linux execs the venv python on bin/cairn.py (outline 5.4.3.8), so one dispatcher serves both platforms.
D2: the red-first proof, one tooth per clause.

D3: bin/cairn.py carries the wiring the bash dispatch carried so exec'ing it drops none: the per-addressed-instance wire (ticket f0ffa0db0952) and the floor's wiring-gap gate on the every-call wire (clause 4).
